title: Normalized scalar tensor constituents and finite evaluation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an inclusion $i$, an algebraic closure $k$ of a finite field of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, and the finite-free restriction assertion $s$ with one fixed integral basis [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction]. Use the canonical coefficient towers $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi^{n+1}$ and $B_n=\mathcal O_L/\pi^{n+1}\mathcal O_L$ and the scalar, tensor and compactification words of [def-coef-system-scalar-projection-data]. For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ and a normalized derived $A_\bullet$-system $M$ whose levels are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, there exist a pure-section and K-flat normalized tensor presentation $\omega$ and a pinned geometric tensor calculus $g$. For every compactification $c$, the restriction of its specified scalar comparison, followed by compact-support restriction, equals $\omega_Y\operatorname{PF}^{c,g}\mathcal F_A^c(\omega_X^{-1})$; its scalar-adjunction transpose equals $\mathcal F_A^c(\eta_M)$ followed by inverse compact-support restriction; and its independently defined open tensor inverse is invertible. For each $c$ and each $n$, there exists finite-level data with the published restriction and pullback evaluation normalizations satisfying the two finite-word/evaluation equations of LevelData.Equation. This assertion does not assert invertibility of the scalar comparison, basis distributivity, or refinement compatibility.

proof.text: Work throughout in the ordinary derived categories of strict systems. By lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction, $T\dashv U$ has unit $\eta_P:P\to UTP$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, restriction commutes with the geometric functors and preserves their units and counits, and $B_\bullet$ is normalized with constructible Tor-amplitude-zero levels. Fix the reduced basis $(b_i)_{i=1}^d$. Its inclusion and coordinate maps give inverse isomorphisms $UTP\cong P^{\oplus d}$ already on complexes of systems: $(x_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i x_i\otimes b_i$. They commute with transitions because all $b_i$ are reductions of the same elements of $S$. Thus this identification holds after localization, with no bound on the complex. In subsequent formulas suppress only these specified restriction/geometry identifications.

proof.text: For the actual coefficient ring sheaf map, ordinary extension followed by restriction identifies with ordinary tensor by the restricted coefficient unit via pure sections z tensor x mapped to x tensor z. The fixed finite-free basis makes the coefficient module flat; the comparison therefore extends degreewise to total K-flat representatives. The scalar model counit and tensor model comparison give the derived natural isomorphism and its specified representative formula. Apply the semilinear geometric calculus to constant coefficient towers; sectionwise pullback identifies coefficients and their transitions, and adjunction conjugation pins pullback and both finite adjunctions to the published operations. These are precisely TensorPresentation and GeometryFamily.

Let $H\in D(\mathscr S_{A,\overline V})$. The restriction compatibility of geometric adjunctions identifies the $p_A^*\dashv Rp_{*,A}$ transpose of $U(a_{p,H})$ with the restriction of its defining $B$-geometric transpose. Under $UT(-)=(-)\otimes^L B_\bullet$, this is exactly
$$p_A^*(Rp_{*,A}H\otimes^L B_{\bullet,W})\xrightarrow{\mu_p}p_A^*Rp_{*,A}H\otimes^L B_{\bullet,\overline V}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{p,A,H}\otimes1}H\otimes^L B_{\bullet,\overline V}.$$
Indeed tensoring the counit acts on the first factor and leaves the coefficient factor unchanged; the canonical pullback/tensor identification has precisely these factors. The adjunction-mate bijection therefore identifies $U(a_{p,H})$ with the specified strict-system proper projection map. This is equality of transposes and hence of maps in the system derived category, before any evaluation.

proof.text:
For the open constituent, $U(b_{j,M})$ is the open tensor comparison: on complexes both balancing maps send a section $x\otimes b$ on the open to that same tensor and send the zero section off the open to zero. The system version and its derived normalization are supplied by lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization. Compose this identity with Step 2 at $H=j_{!,A}M$. The defining proper-then-open word for the system projection transformation gives
$$U(c^c_{h,M})=\operatorname{PF}^{c,\mathrm{sys}}_{h,M,B_\bullet}.$$
Its domain is valid because $M$ is normalized with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels and $B_\bullet$ has these properties by Step 1. Evaluation of the simultaneous operations, their units, counits, tensor identifications and transposes agrees with the ordinary level operations by lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections. Consequently evaluation of this specified $c^c$ is exactly the finite proper-counit/open-balancing comparison. Evaluation is used here only after the system identity has been proved.

proof.text:
Write $\rho^c:\mathcal F^c_{h,A}U\xrightarrow{\sim}U\mathcal F^c_{h,B}$ for the inverse of the specified restriction comparison. We show
$$U(c^c_{h,M})\eta_{\mathcal F^c_{h,A}M}=\rho^c_{T_VM}\mathcal F^c_{h,A}(\eta_M).$$
For the proper constituent, the $p_A^*\dashv Rp_{*,A}$ transpose of $U(a_{p,H})\eta_{Rp_{*,A}H}$ is $(\varepsilon_H\otimes1)p_A^*\eta_{Rp_{*,A}H}=\eta_H\varepsilon_H$: pullback of the scalar unit inserts $1$, so this equality is naturality of $\eta$. The transpose of $Rp_{*,A}(\eta_H)$ is also $\eta_H\varepsilon_H$, by counit naturality. Hence these maps agree, with the restriction comparison inserted. For the open constituent $U(b_{j,M})\eta_{j_!M}=j_!(\eta_M)$ under that comparison: on the open both maps insert $1$, and off it both are zero; exact scalar extension and exact open extension descend this identity of complex maps. Composing the two identities proves the displayed formula. By the stated $T_W\dashv U_W$ bijection $a\mapsto U(a)\eta$, it says exactly that $c^c$ is the scalar-adjunction mate of $\rho^c$. No faithfulness assertion for $U$ on derived morphisms enters.
